home.headline: How to Change the World
home.subheadline: Plan change initiatives using Jurgen Appelo's 4-facet framework from Management 3.0.
home.framework_body: "How to Change the World" (Appelo) teaches that successful change requires working across four facets simultaneously: the system, the people, the network, and the environment. Most change failures come from focusing on only one or two.

dance.label: Dance with the System
dance.description: Understand how the current system works. Map feedback loops, incentives, and constraints. Work with the system, not against it.
prompts: What feedback loops maintain the status quo?
What are the key leverage points for change?
How can you iterate rather than big-bang?
What metrics will show whether the system is changing?

mind.label: Mind the People
mind.description: People's intrinsic motivators, fears, and mental models drive whether change succeeds or fails. Engage them, don't manage them.
prompts: Who are the early adopters and who are the resistors?
What motivates each key stakeholder intrinsically?
What fears or concerns do people have about this change?
How will you acknowledge and address those concerns?

stimulate.label: Stimulate the Network
stimulate.description: Change spreads through social networks. Identify connectors, communities of practice, and influence channels. Grow the movement.
prompts: Who are the connectors and influencers in this network?
What communities of practice can amplify the change?
How can you make early successes visible to others?
What stories or rituals will reinforce the new behaviors?

change.label: Change the Environment
change.description: The environment shapes behavior. Modify incentives, constraints, tools, and physical/digital spaces to make the desired behavior easier.
prompts: What incentives currently reward the old behavior?
What constraints or rules need to change?
What new tools, spaces, or structures would support the change?
How can you make the new behavior the path of least resistance?

learn.title: About the Framework
learn.intro: "How to Change the World" is a practical guide by Jurgen Appelo (Management 3.0) that synthesizes complexity science, psychology, and systems thinking into a practical approach for change agents.
learn.why_body: Most change efforts fail because they focus on just one thing — usually the system or just the people. Real change is complex and requires working simultaneously across all four dimensions. The facets reinforce each other: environmental changes make new behaviors easier, network effects spread adoption, motivated people sustain the effort, and system adjustments remove structural barriers.
learn.tip1: Start with small, reversible experiments rather than big plans.
learn.tip2: Identify 2–3 key people per facet — you can't engage everyone.
learn.tip3: Track leading indicators (behaviors) not just lagging ones (outcomes).
learn.tip4: Celebrate small wins visibly to stimulate the network.
learn.tip5: Review and adapt the plan every 2–4 weeks.
